messages:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT P1: eu-west-1 GPU pool approaching 98% utilisation. Autoscaler attempted scaleup x3 but failed. Queue depth for inference requests > 5k and growing. Pager to #incidents -> @amber oncall.

amber: oncall here, ack. joining bridge in 60s. @chris @maya pls standby. any customer impact reports?

chris: seeing sustained enqueue rate spike after 09:12 UTC. controller logs show: 
```
scale_attempt: 2026-03-15T09:13:02Z -> provider error: QuotaExceeded: Request quota for gpu-instances exceeded for account
scale_attempt: 2026-03-15T09:13:07Z -> provider error: RateLimitExceeded
```

maya: I'm on metrics. queue_growth_5m = +3.2k, latency P95 now 15s token, 503s started at 09:17 for low-tier customers. Noting dedicated pools still healthy.

leo: quick note: reserve pool in eu-west-1 is currently at zero; we had a CI job in morning that released standby nodes. trying rapid-provision to warmup-standby.

amber: triage plan: (1) reduce ingress for non-paid/free tiers (2) enable routing to fallback-model-eu (smaller variant) (3) attempt manual scale with provider support contact. chris/maya, carry execs. alex, prep CS notice template.

chris: started manual scale request to provider via infra-runbook script: `./provision_gpu.sh --region eu-west-1 --count 8 --type a100` -> currently pending. Provider console shows quota soft-limit. Opening support ticket, escalated.

maya: throttling rule applied to route:posting-rate limiter -> non-premium keys set to 20r/s. That should reduce new enqueues. Observing drop in enqueue by ~40% already.

incidents-bot: NOTE: automated fallback to quantized-small model was attempted at 09:21 UTC, 65% of requests successfully routed, 35% failed due to compat issues.

amber: good. chris, can we enable cross-region fallback to eu-north? latency hit but better than 503s.

chris: eu-north has spare capacity but models there are missing a few newer weights. I can enable model-variant fallback -> will send traffic to eu-north for older model snapshot which is compatible. Doing a canary at 09:26.

leo: warming standby pool via internal API: `POST /internal/pools/warm?region=eu-west-1&count=6` -> job accepted. ETA ~4m.

julia: any customer-facing impact yet? alex?

alex: CS seeing increased error reports from two enterprise customers and multiple PLG users. Putting a brief note on status page: "Degraded performance and intermittent errors in eu-west-1 inference — mitigation in progress". Inbound priority tickets opened.

maya: after throttling and fallback, queue growth plateaued at +200, latency P95 down to 8s, error-rate to free-tier down 70%. Manual scale still blocked by provider quota.

chris: provider responded: they can grant temporary quota bump if we sign emergency form + phone confirmation. I've escalated to provider-SRE inbox; they asked for expected usage and termination window.

amber: do we want to accept quota with commitment (1h) to unblocking? pros/cons?

julia: yes accept. we need stability for customers. ensure we tear down after. chris/leo coordinate.

chris: accepted and provider granted soft-bump +8 gpus at 09:33 UTC. Manual provisioning succeeded; nodes joined cluster at 09:37. Autoscaler still noisy, but new capacity reduced queue depth by ~2.3k.

incidents-bot: BRIDGE UPDATE: Bridge created by amber at 09:14 UTC — https://call.example/bridge/1771234568

amber: immediate mitigations recap: throttled non-paid traffic, enabled quantized fallback, manual provider quota bump + manual scale, warmed standby pool. Current status: degraded -> partial service restored. Keeping page open for 45m to ensure stability.

maya: monitoring: token cost spike but within budget. No further provider errors after 09:40. We'll keep autoscaler logs on debug for 6h.

alex: CS message updated with ETA for full recovery and note we've routed some traffic to fallback models. Sales notified for impacted enterprise customers.

chris: quick root-cause hypothesis: sudden load spike combined with zero standby buffer + autoscaler not retrying on transient quota errors. Also provider quota enforcement was strict (no queue for burst).

amber: agreed. action items captured here. I'll open a follow-up postmortem thread but listing immediate action items now.

julia: list them so we can assign: 
1) Add provider-quota-aware retry logic to autoscaler (owner: chris)
2) Ensure minimum standby buffer for each region (owner: leo)
3) Improve monitoring & alerting for provider quota exhaustion (owner: maya)
4) Runbook update: explicit provider escalation steps and support contact template (owner: chris)
5) Customer comms playbook for degraded/inflight fallback (owner: alex)
6) Add traffic-shaping default policy for free/PLG tiers (owner: product/devex)

amber: assigning provisional due dates: 1) 2 weeks, 2) 1 week, 3) 3 days, 4) 3 days, 5) 24h, 6) product to triage. If anyone wants to reassign ping me.

maya: capturing log snippets for postmortem and uploading to case. Also saving autoscaler debug trace: `autoscaler::attempt(3) -> provider_quota_error -> backoff policy skipped incorrectly`

chris: will follow up with PR for autoscaler retry logic and provider error classification.

amber: ok team, closing active page at 10:00 UTC, keeping an action-item tracking doc. Postmortem to be drafted by chris + maya, reviewers: julia + amber. Due by Friday.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: 1771234568 at 10:00 UTC — condition: queue < 200 and error-rate < baseline.

alex: sending customer follow-ups now.

julia: thanks all — good coordination. We'll review timeline in postmortem and ensure capacity buffer is prioritized.

chris: uploading related logs and tickets to incident tracker. PR preview soon.

maya: I'll keep watch on the fallback routing overnight.

amber: good work. end thread."
